summary: The Machine, real. New workbench/machine_real.py reads and changes removable storage (udisks2), power (UPower) and the network and Wi-Fi (NetworkManager) over QtDBus, sound through wpctl and screens through xrandr. Each section says "Not available on this computer" and why when its service is absent. New workbench/machine_room_qt.py puts five rows at the top of the Machine tab: Storage, Power, Network, Sound, Screens, each with its few words. Under them stay the overview rows that still mean something: Processor, Memory, Devices, Installed tools; the disks and mounts sit under Storage, the interfaces under Network. Each of the five rows opens a page in the centre with its controls: Mount, Open in Files, Unmount, Eject safely ("SAFE TO REMOVE" only after it is read back); battery and mains; networking and Wi-Fi on/off, the networks heard, Join (the password goes to NetworkManager in the call), Disconnect; volume, mute, output; modes, primary, on/off, mirror/extend with "Keep this arrangement?" and an automatic go-back after 15 s. Changes happen only on the owner's press, run off the window's thread, and are said DONE only when read back. One read-only Kernel operation, machine.state, lets her observe the machine. With stand-ins the smoke passed 42 of 42 checks, and the window run did each step by pressing its button.

existing_tests_changed: tools/check_machine_ui.py (a window check, not run by the owner's rule): Machine's children are now Storage, Power, Network, Sound, Screens, Processor, Memory, Devices, Installed tools (was Processor, Memory, Storage, Connections, Devices, Installed tools); its loop skips rows that hold no overview section and a drive row under Storage; the overview's connections are page.items['network'] (was 'connections'). Nothing else changed in it.
decisions: PySide6 cannot read QtDBus maps: beginMapEntry and endArray share their signature with the writing ones, so PySide6 calls the writing ones. machine_real.plain() reads each map entry on a copy of the map's reader (a copy reads on from the same place) and steps the map's reader over the entry. Checked in an experiment and the smoke against a{oa{sa{sv}}}, a{sv}, ao, aay and (uu). NetworkManager's a{sa{sv}} is sent as a QDBusArgument built with beginMap/appendVariant.

The Wi-Fi password: the owner types it into a password field on the Network page. It goes to NetworkManager once, in AddAndActivateConnection (802-11-wireless-security.psk, NetworkManager keeps it with the saved connection). The field is cleared at once and Graphite writes, logs and keeps nothing. Graphite does not register as a NetworkManager secret agent: PySide6 cannot export a GetSecrets that returns a{sa{sv}}, and a Fluxbox session has no other agent. A network NetworkManager has saved is joined with its saved connection, with no password asked. If a connection that Join just added then fails, Join deletes it. Enterprise (802.1X) and WEP networks are refused with words that name nmtui.

Changes are not Kernel operations: Mount, Eject, Join, the volume, the screens and the rest are module functions called on the owner's press, so the model cannot dispatch them. Only machine.state (read) is registered, for her observation. K3 may wrap the functions in grants.

Bus: GRAPHITE_MACHINE_BUS=session (or bus='session') reads udisks2, UPower and NetworkManager from the session bus; the default is the system bus. udisks2 is D-Bus-activated on Debian, so a service that is only activatable counts as there.

Screens are read with xrandr --current, so a refresh never makes the X server probe the outputs again. A change to the screens is undone after 15 s unless the owner presses Keep. The last screen that is on is never turned off.

The rows refresh every 10 s while the Machine tab shows. An open page reads again every 3 s and is drawn again only when what it read has changed. It never redraws while the password field or a mode list has the focus, or while Keep is waiting. Row tooltips use the last reading and never read again themselves.
Unlocking an encrypted drive is not offered: it would take the passphrase through Graphite. Such a drive shows LOCKED, with words saying the system's own tools can unlock it.
Percentages from a battery or the volume are read as decimal digits (Decimal, then an int); no float is used in any decision.
findings_for_the_coordinator: F2: the machine's reads run on the window's thread. That is several D-Bus round trips and two wpctl runs plus one xrandr run every 10 s while the Machine tab shows, and every 3 s for an open page. They are fast with the services present and instant when absent; F2 may move them to a worker. The changes already run off the thread.

S5 (Settings): the S4 functions to reach are in machine_real: storage, mount, unmount, eject; power; network, set_networking, set_wifi, scan, join, disconnect; sound, set_volume, set_mute, set_output; screens, change_screens(change, name, mode), put_back. A page opens with machine_room_qt.show(host, key).
S5: with lxpolkit in the session, udisks2 and NetworkManager may show the system's own permission prompt. Changes wait up to 120 s for it, on a worker thread.
K2 and K3: machine.state is the observation. Wrapping the change functions in grants is future work; for now they are owner-only by construction.
Registry regenerated (855 operations, + machine.state). MANIFEST.json and the seed were not touched.

Each opens a page in the centre. When a service is missing, the row and the page say "not available on this computer" and why.
